notes: Tesla publishes no state, country or regional breakdown of employees, stores, service centers or Supercharger sites in its FY2025 10-K or its quarterly Update decks; both give only global totals, so countries and regions are null. Sites are the eight primary manufacturing facilities in FY2025 10-K Item 2 (unchanged from the prior year) plus the Austin headquarters. Vehicle-factory capacity figures come from the newest quarterly Update deck, Q3 2026 (installed capacity, not production; Tesla's IR files moved from digitalassets.tesla.com to assets-ir.tesla.com). In Q3 2026 the California line shows only Model 3 / Model Y (>550,000; Model S / Model X no longer listed), Texas Model Y rose to >375,000 and Cybercab shows >125,000 in production; the deck also shows Tesla Semi at 25,000 in Nevada and Megafactory Texas beginning production, which are not added as sites. Gigafactory Shanghai and Megafactory Shanghai: Tesla owns the buildings and holds 50-year land use rights. The 'employees' metric (IHS Markit's 2018–2021 California study, commissioned by Tesla) has no rows: one state cannot make a state map and the figure is old; no newer Tesla state study was found (checked 2026-11-24). Tesla also hosts a 'Gigafactory Nevada Economic and Fiscal Impact Analysis 2022' (Applied Analysis), whose headcounts combine Tesla with on-site vendors and indirect and induced jobs, so no Tesla-only Nevada figure is recorded. Period: 10-K as of Dec 31, 2025; capacity as of Q3 2026.
